# FDGD021

> NOT PERMITTED: Adding `abstract` Members

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section D.7.2 Adding abstract Members. Can cause: runtime and compilation breaks.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Breaks every derived type that is not `abstract`. PublicApiAnalyzers (optional in /fdg-setup) can flag changes to the public API.

## From the book

If you add a new `abstract` member to a type, then any derived types that were not already declared as `abstract` will fail to initialize; a `TypeLoadException` will display a message indicating that the new member “does not have an implementation.”

Non-`abstract` derived types will fail to compile due to not providing an implementation for the new member.

The .NET BCL team considers this an unacceptable breaking change.
